tasks.short: Patrol the courthouse and escort court staff

steps.what: Patrol the actual courthouse interior and exterior, observe conditions and respond to security concerns under the court's existing procedures.
Escort judges and other court employees as actually required, maintain awareness of the people and surroundings and coordinate directly with court security staff.
Write the actual patrol or escort exceptions in the existing court security log {OTHER}, checking the completed entry for factual accuracy and the correct event references.
outputs: checked final patrol and escort log entry

steps.what: Save the checked final patrol and escort log entry in the court security log {OTHER}.
inputs: checked final patrol and escort log entry

tasks.design: Keep physical patrol and escort work with the bailiff. The actual security-log entry is separate; existing native event fields are assumed adequate and no further reduction is established.
tasks.previous_blocker: Physical presence and direct coordination provide the security service.
tasks.enabler_now: A native log can hold actual exceptions but cannot perform the patrol or escort.
tasks.still_hard: Changing people and courthouse conditions require immediate judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Recognise and respond to a real security concern in context.

ambition.what: No automatic patrol or escort decisions.

reach.learn: Communicate actual observations and handovers clearly.

evidence.claim: An event log records observations but does not replace the physical security presence of a court officer.

assumptions: Boundary is actual courthouse patrol and staff escort with the existing exception-log entry. Log writing and save are separated before choosing zero. Shares are illustrative for work where this log already exists, not a new mandatory report.

The bailiff observes the actual patrol or escort and manually supplies location, event date/time, relevant event reference, observed concern and actual response in s3. Capture and factual checking remain fully counted. Scheduled patrol or escort assignments do not establish completion.

Native event fields are already used in this scenario. A model-generated account would still require full factual verification and no labour reduction is assumed. No new surveillance or tracking is proposed.

s3's ordinary check of the completed entry supplies the requested s4 gate without added approval work. Changes require rechecking; save retains its one-share time. No new software means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Actual security-log duties and current native fields
research_questions: Does any actual duplicate event entry remain beyond the existing log?

already_counted.description: Write and check the actual security exception entry.

approvals.approved_version: Final patrol and escort entry checked at the end of s3

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Patrol, escort, actual log writing and save remain separately counted. No specific additional change to the existing native log or physical work is established.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Observe actual courtroom behaviour and determine whether smoking, disturbance or another breach of the court's rules requires a warning or action under the court's direction.
Warn the person about smoking or disturbing court procedure, enforce the courtroom's behaviour rules within existing authority and respond to the person's actual behaviour.
outputs: delivered warning and actual enforcement response

tasks.design: Keep direct observation and the live warning with the bailiff. No repeatable document lookup or record-writing duty is established for each ordinary warning, so no administrative saving is invented.
tasks.previous_blocker: Maintaining courtroom order depends on live behaviour and the court's direction.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing rules explain authority but do not replace the live interaction.
tasks.still_hard: Misunderstanding, distress and disruption require proportionate human judgement.
tasks.human_edge: Respond to the person and circumstances rather than treating every disruption identically.
tasks.altitude: No demonstrated change to the work.

reach.learn: Use clear instructions under the responsible authority.

evidence.claim: A rule reference does not provide the contextual observation and live communication needed to maintain courtroom order.

assumptions: Boundary includes observing a breach, deciding the response and delivering the actual warning. The statement requires no separate document or digital send for each warning. No hypothetical report-writing baseline is added; when a real incident requires an existing security-log entry, its actual work belongs to that incident record rather than being hidden in this conversation.
The bailiff directly observes the behaviour. No structured violation code or automated assessment is assumed. A template or native view does not shorten the actual warning in this scenario.
No new software, record or approval process is introduced; incremental upkeep is zero. All physical and interpersonal work remains fully counted.
research_questions: Which warnings actually require a separate incident record under current practice?

already_counted.description: Observe the actual behaviour and decide the appropriate response.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: No specific software change shortens direct observation or the actual warning. No routine report or repeated lookup is established to remove.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

tasks.short: Report an actual need for police or medical assistance

steps.what: Observe the actual situation and identify the need for police or medical assistance, the courthouse location and the facts available to report without assuming a diagnosis or outcome.
outputs: actual assistance need and incident facts

steps.what: Select the existing emergency contact for the sheriff's office or its local court-security equivalent and confirm the actual incident location and assistance request to be communicated.
inputs: actual assistance need and incident facts
outputs: checked current assistance request and contact

steps.what: Report the actual need for police or medical assistance to the selected office by the existing phone or radio channel, give the checked location and facts and answer the recipient's immediate questions.
inputs: checked current assistance request and contact
outputs: delivered assistance request and recipient response

tasks.design: Keep the assistance report as the existing direct emergency call or radio exchange. Contact selection and the actual report are explicit, with no new form, model or approval delay.
tasks.previous_blocker: The recipient needs timely, accurate facts about a changing incident.
tasks.enabler_now: Existing emergency channels already deliver the report directly.
tasks.still_hard: The bailiff must communicate uncertainty and respond to live questions.
tasks.human_edge: Report what was actually observed and identify an urgent need without overstating the facts.
tasks.altitude: No demonstrated change to the reporting work.

reach.learn: Communicate observed condition and location clearly.

evidence.claim: A direct emergency phone or radio exchange supports immediate clarification of observed incident facts.

assumptions: Boundary includes the actual assistance report and immediate recipient questions, not merely noticing the incident. The US sheriff's-office wording maps only to the existing authorised local contact; no jurisdictional power is invented. No additional written report is presumed.

The bailiff directly produces actual location, observed situation, assistance need and available incident facts in s1 and checks the current request/contact in s2. This is the normal live communication decision, not an added permission stage or waiting process. The requested send gate binds those checked facts and destination when the call begins; new facts are communicated and checked live by the bailiff.

Native contact access is already available. There is no repeated data entry to remove, and an AI draft would not replace the live report. No software or recurring upkeep is introduced, so incremental work is zero.
unknowns: Local emergency contact and radio procedures
research_questions: Is the existing emergency contact immediately accessible without a new reporting form?

already_counted.description: Confirm the current request and correct emergency contact.

approvals.approved_version: Current assistance request, observed facts and contact checked in s2 immediately before the live report

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Observation, contact confirmation and the actual assistance report are separately retained. No specific change reduces their labour or introduces a new written baseline.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

steps.what: Physically check the courtroom for security and cleanliness, identify actual deficiencies and address or refer them through the court's existing arrangements.
outputs: actual security and cleanliness check outcome

steps.what: Inspect and count the actual notepads and other sundry supplies needed by the judge, jurors and attorneys, identifying what is missing at the point of use.
Obtain the missing sundry supplies from existing stock and place them for actual courtroom use, checking that the needed items are present.

tasks.design: Keep the physical readiness inspection, actual supply count and replenishment with the bailiff. No separate inventory application or routine report is established to remove in this small point-of-use supply task.
tasks.previous_blocker: Security, cleanliness and supplies must be checked at the actual courtroom.
tasks.enabler_now: A digital list could display requirements but cannot establish current physical condition.
tasks.still_hard: Unexpected deficiencies need observation and practical resolution.
tasks.human_edge: Notice that the courtroom is not ready despite a planned checklist.

ambition.what: No inferred room readiness or stock.

reach.learn: Separate actual inspection from planned readiness.

evidence.claim: A requirements list does not measure the physical condition or supply availability of a courtroom.

assumptions: Boundary includes actual security and cleanliness inspection, actual stock observation and placing available supplies. Supply counting is separated before choosing zero. The statement does not establish a transactional inventory ledger or routine report for notepads; none is invented. If an actual purchasing request or incident record is required, its existing work must be modelled for that case.

The bailiff directly observes current condition and actual supply availability in s1-s2. No machine-readable stock count, automatic consumption record or completion flag is assumed. Physical replenishment remains fully counted.

Native checklist access is considered but no repeated list reconstruction or record entry is established. A checklist cannot replace the physical checks. No new process or approval activity means zero incremental upkeep.
unknowns: Actual local supply and checklist practices
research_questions: Is there any genuine duplicate supply-record entry in the current point-of-use process?

already_counted.description: Observe actual supply quantities and shortages.

time_saved_range_pct.basis: Actual room inspection, supply counting and replenishment are separately retained. No repeated report or inventory-entry baseline is established to remove.

tasks.savings_basis: 100 focal-role baseline hours; external labour excluded; incremental focal work deducted once; provisional

role.altitude: Bailiffs retain physical courthouse security, live communication and readiness checks; the actual record and report duties remain explicitly counted.
reach: Coordinate actual courthouse conditions with security guards
Communicate assistance needs clearly to emergency personnel
role.ambitious_version: Maintain clear, factual security communications without substituting scheduled activity or generated text for actual courthouse observations.
